summary: Manages a growable buffer (pointer at 0x0, capacity at 0x4, stored size at 0x8). If a3 exceeds capacity, frees the old buffer and allocates a new one of size a3. When the buffer is non-null and a3 is positive, copies a3 bytes from a2 into it and records the stored size; otherwise records stored size 0. Returns 1 in both paths.

operations.description: If requested size a3 is greater than current capacity (this+4), the buffer must be reallocated.
If an old buffer exists at this+0, free it via FreeWrapper_7bcf.
Allocate a new buffer of size a3 via OperatorNewWithResultCheck, storing the result into this+0.
Update capacity (this+4) to the new size a3.
If the buffer at this+0 is non-null and a3 is positive, copy a3 bytes from a2 into it and record stored size a3 at this+8.
On the copy path, set stored size (this+8) to a3.
On the skip path (null buffer or non-positive size), set stored size (this+8) to 0.
Return 1 on the copy path and on the skip path (skip is not an error).

unresolved: The stored-size field at this+8 appears in a growable-buffer pattern shared with the caller MemcpyLikeWithRealloc-style buffers; exact struct layout (allocation header versus pure data buffer) is unconfirmed.
Allocation failure inside OperatorNewWithResultCheck is not explicitly guarded in this function, so behavior when the allocator reports failure is inferred, not evidenced.
Field at this+0 is read from and written to across the realloc path; the init_literal 0 recorded for this+8 comes from the skip-path assignment only.
